newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips appoints senior marketing director.
newsitem.headline: Philips appoints senior marketing director.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Thursday it had appointed Gerard Dufour as its senior director of marketing.
Philips said its chief executive officer Cor Boonstra had underlined the importance of this new post in a letter to the Philips staff.

"We need to dramatically improve our collective ability to anticipate, meet and even exceed the demands of the market," Boonstra wrote in his letter. He added this required "a further radical approach" towards Philips' processes and mindset in which customers' interests should drive the group's business.
Philips said Dufour would, as a "custodian" for the Philips brand name, be responsible for improving the quality and creativity of Philips' marketing policy, activities and communications.
He will also take charge of the group's corporate marketing communications department.

Earlier this week Philips warned that its operating profits were unlikely to recover in the second half of this year, as it had previously expected. It said it would accelerate action for recovery, which prompted expectations that the company would need further reorganisations.

Financial analysts said further restructurings would be a logical step for Boonstra, who took over the chairmanship on October 1, now the first set of results to be published under his reign were to be disappointing.

On Tuesday, Philips announced it would reorganise its head office in Eindhoven and added job cuts were unavoidable. Over 800 people are now working at the centre, covering financial, legal, fiscal, press office and other administrative posts.
